_comment: Transport security on the AWS side of the boundary, and the findings the at-rest checks
cannot see. A bucket encrypted with a customer-managed key that hands its contents to a
plaintext HTTP request is the pairing that makes reporting at-rest encryption alone
actively misleading — northwind-public-assets is exactly that.
edge/80 redirects and warns rather than failing: no application data crosses in the clear,
though the request line does. reports/80 forwards to a target group and fails. stream/9000
is raw TCP, where TLS may terminate on the target and no describe call can tell, so it is
reported as not evaluated rather than resolved either way.
legacy/443 is the version finding: ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08 reads as a security policy and
permits TLS 1.0. canary/443 carries a policy name this harness does not recognise and warns,
because a policy AWS published after this collector was written is exactly where a silent
For KSI-SVC-VCM the population is the declaration, not the estate: internal-api is declared
machine-to-machine and has mutual authentication off, mesh verifies against a trust store,
and decommissioned-api is declared but no longer exists — the declaration and the estate
disagreeing, which nothing here can resolve into a removal or a rename.
